paper_title: Iron-Catalyzed Aerobic Oxidation of Aldehydes: Single Component Catalyst and Mechanistic Studies

questions.question: In this paper, what compound does the label '1a' refer to?
What is the chemical identity/name given in the paper for Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, the catalyst used in the study?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Fe(NO3)3·9H2O — iron(III) nitrate nonahydrate (used as the single-component catalyst)

questions.question: Under the standard conditions for the aerobic oxidation of aldehyde 1a (Table 1, entry 7), what solvent, catalyst loading, temperature, reaction time, and oxygen source were used?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Anhydrous MeCN as solvent; 5 mol% Fe(NO3)3·9H2O; 25 °C; 12 h; oxygen supplied from a bag of molecular O2.

questions.question: Which gave the higher NMR yield of carboxylic acid 2a: using 5 mol% Fe(NO3)3·9H2O alone (Table 1, entry 3) or using FeCl3·6H2O as the metal salt (Table 2, entry 7)? Provide both yields reported in the paper.
questions.ground_truth_answer: Fe(NO3)3·9H2O alone (Table 1, entry 3) gave 64% NMR yield of 2a; FeCl3·6H2O (Table 2, entry 7) gave 52% yield — Fe(NO3)3·9H2O gave the higher yield.

questions.question: What isolated yield and 1H NMR data are reported in the experimental section for carboxylic acid 2a (dodecanoic acid)?
